newsitem.title: USA: US Conference Bd--rate hike won't quash confidence.
newsitem.headline: US Conference Bd--rate hike won't quash confidence.

text.p: Any ratcheting up of short-term U.S. interest rates by the Federal Reserve won't temper soaring U.S. consumer confidence, said Ken Goldstein, an economist at The Conference Board.

Speaking to Reuters Financial Television after The Conference Board released its March report on consumer attitudes, Goldstein said: "The rate hike won't quash (confidence). What it might do is keep it from rising still higher."

The Fed is meeting Tuesday in Washington to decide the near-term course of monetary policy. Experts widely expect central bankers to raise interest rates by 25 basis points on the overnight bank lending, or federal funds rate.
Goldstein said the U.S. economy does not need reining in via an interest rate hike. However, if it did, he said, a mere 25 basis points would not be enough to slow the huge U.S. economic engine.
"I don't think it needs slowing," Goldstein said. "If it does, a quarter-point move is not enough to slow down this $7.0 trillion economy."
